subject: DPA: request for sensitive-field carveout and pseudonymization approach
messages:
From: Alice Green <alice.green@horizonbio.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@horizonbio.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: sensitive fields & pseudonymization carveout

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for taking this. As we review the DPA redline from your legal team we hit one blocker from product/analytics: Horizon's pipelines rely on a short-lived hashed customer_id field and a couple of telemetry attributes (model_variant, prompt_category) to de-duplicate and measure pipeline health. The proposed DPA language appears to ban retention of any persistent identifiers and broad telemetry exports.

We're asking for a narrow carveout: allow retention of a hashed customer_id (salted and rotation friendly), allow KV cache snapshot exports for debugging (only when explicitly requested and stored in our S3), and permit pseudonymized telemetry (no raw content, only derived labels). We can accept strict deletion TTLs and auditability.

Attached: Horizon-Pipeline-Requirements.pdf (short spec). Can Redwood confirm if this is technically feasible and what security controls you need to sign off before legal will accept the carveout?

Thanks,
Alice Green
Senior Product Manager, Horizon Bio
alice.green@horizonbio.com

Alice—thanks, and appreciate the clear ask and the attachment. Looping in Security (Olga) and Product (Karthik) so we can scope the risk and propose precise contract language. Also putting Marissa (legal) on copy for redline coordination.

High-level reaction (product): we generally avoid persisting raw identifiers, but salted hashes for dedupe and short retention TTLs are something we've agreed to several times with customers. KV snapshots are trickier — we can produce them only as on-demand exports, encrypted, and stored in a Horizon-controlled bucket or your dedicated bucket behind a customer KMS.

Questions for Security/Product to sign off on before Legal drafts language: 
- Can Security require customer-side KMS for snapshot storage?
- Will Product accept a 90-day TTL default for hashed ids with option for 30/60/90?
- Can we commit to not using any retained identifier for model training or improvement?

If Security and Product can confirm, I will propose a short DPA carveout paragraph and a one-click DocuSign amendment. Timeline: Horizon would like this resolved in the next two weeks.

Thanks for raising — flagged for Security review. Short answers up front: possible, with constraints. Attached is a checklist of controls we will require.

Security constraints and asks (must be contractually required):
- Explicit list of allowed subprocessors and a requirement to notify Horizon of changes 30 days prior; allow review for high-risk subprocs.
- Use of customer-managed KMS for any persisted snapshot; snapshots must be encrypted with a key Horizon controls.
- Retention windows pinned in DPA (max 90 days for hashed identifiers; default 30 days unless customer selects otherwise).
- Audit logging for access to snapshots and a monthly export of access logs for the customer for 12 months.
- Hard prohibition on using retained identifiers or snapshots for any model training, A/B experiments, or offline feature store ingestion — contractual guarantee and an operational check.

Operational workaround for KV snapshots: we can enable on-demand snapshot export via a job that runs during a scheduled maintenance window. Product should confirm performance and availability constraints.

Please see attached security-eval-checklist.xlsx for specifics (controls we will insist on in the DPA exhibit). If Product (Karthik) can confirm feasibility and call out perf delta, Security will prepare the contract language and a short audit playbook.

—Olga
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: DPA: sensitive fields & pseudonymization carveout

Thanks — technical feasibility summary from Product/RTE: we can implement the requested controls with minimal runtime changes and one small rollout risk. Details: 

1) Hashed ID retention: implement hashed customer_id with rolling salt, persistent only in a limited TTL cache (e.g., Redis layer with enforced expiry). TTLs 30/60/90 configurable per-customer via route config; default 30 days. Impact: negligible storage cost, no model-training pipeline access.

2) KV snapshot exports: we will enable a gated export job that produces encrypted snapshots (prefix-only data + metadata labels) and writes to an external S3 location provided by Horizon (preferred). If customer S3 is not provided, we can store snapshots in Redwood infra but must use customer-managed KMS. Export is asynchronous and can be scheduled; expected latency during snapshot generation may add 50-200ms tail to affected requests while snapshotting is in flight — we will limit concurrent snapshots.

3) Telemetry pseudonymization: we will scrub PII and only emit derived labels (prompt_category, model_variant). We will also ensure telemetry is tagged with a one-way hash. No downstream features or training pipelines will consume these hashes.

Perf note: across benchmarked workloads with short prompts, the guarded export path increases p50 by ~1–3% and p95 by ~4–6% when snapshotting concurrently. We can gate exports to maintenance windows for latency-sensitive routes.

Operational asks back to Security/Legal: provide the exact retention windows and audit log retention SLA you require so we can bake them into the route config and the DPA exhibit. JIRA: INF-1842 will track the work (link in thread).

—Karthik
Product Manager, Runtime

Alice — thank you, team — below is the proposed compromise and next steps so Horizon can get legal signoff quickly: 

Proposed DPA exhibit paragraph (draft):
"Redwood may persist pseudonymized identifiers (salted one-way hashes of customer identifiers) for the sole purpose of request de-duplication and operational debugging. Such identifiers will be retained for a contractually agreed TTL (default 30 days, configurable to 60 or 90 days) and will not be used for model training or product analytics beyond operational telemetry. KV cache snapshots will only be produced on-demand, encrypted with customer-managed KMS and stored in an external customer S3 bucket when provided; otherwise snapshots will be encrypted with customer-managed KMS in Redwood's storage. Access to snapshots will be audit-logged and monthly access reports provided to the customer for a period of 12 months. Redwood will maintain an up-to-date list of subprocessors and will notify the customer 30 days in advance of changes to high-risk subprocessors."

Action items / timeline: 
- Security (Olga) to confirm the final DPA exhibit wording and attach the checklist Marissa can use in the redline (by EOD Tue).
- Product (Karthik) to update INF-1842 with the TTL config and perf caveats and provide acceptance criteria (by Wed).
- Legal (Marissa) to draft the amendment and DocuSign link for Horizon (by Thu).

If Horizon accepts the above paragraph, I will route the DocuSign and mark deal DBL-4729 as pending-execution. Please confirm by EOD Thursday so we can meet your two-week timeline.
